newsitem.title: TURKEY: Another Turkish MP quits pro-Islamist alliance.
newsitem.headline: Another Turkish MP quits pro-Islamist alliance.

text.p: Another Turkish MP has resigned from the ruling pro-Islamist alliance, further boosting prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz's hopes of winning a confidence vote for his secularist government.
"We haven't been able to secure stability in parliament. That is why I have made this move, aimed at uniting the right," Anatolian quoted deputy Evren Bulut as saying on Saturday night.
He became the tenth True Path Party member to quit the conservative party in less than a week in protest at its alliance with the Islam-based Welfare Party.
The resignees are expected to vote for fellow rightist Yilmaz at a key parliamentary test in the planned secularist coalition government within two weeks.
Yilmaz now has 276 votes on paper, compared to True Path and the Islamists who can command the support of 271 MPs.
He was asked by the president to find a new government after Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, resigned earlier this month.
